newsitem.title: USA: Florida seeks disaster aid for freeze damage.
newsitem.headline: Florida seeks disaster aid for freeze damage.

text.p: Governor Lawton Chiles has asked the U.S. Agriculture Department to declare 20 Florida counties disaster areas after last weekend's hard freeze damaged winter vegetables and citrus crops throughout the state.

Temperatures fell as low as 19 degrees Fahrenheit in central and south Florida last weekend, causing "significant damage" to winter vegetables, citrus, pasture lands and nursery plants, Chiles said in a statement.

"While citrus losses are still being assessed, early reports indicate 10 to 35 percent of the crop being affected in certain counties," the governor said in his letter, which was sent to the USDA late Thursday.
Florida citrus growers have been examining groves since last weekend to try and estimate the amount of damage to young trees and oranges yet to be harvested.
Miami's Dade County has estimated its vegetable losses at $95 million, and total statewide losses could top $270 million, Chiles said.
More than 50 percent of South Florida's winter vegetable crop was damaged by the freeze, with hardest hit crops being tomatoes, green beans, squash, bell peppers, eggplant, sweet corn and zucchini.

Earlier this week, Florida officials said consumers could expect vegetable prices to increase because of the devastated crop. Some supermarkets have marked up produce prices by as much as 50 percent since the weekend.
